newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Oct 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Oct 28.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Eastern Cape's government would stop using the electronic payment system within the next two months to clamp down on teachers fraudulently drawing salaries, Deputy President Thabo Mbeki said last week.

- Private credit growth rose in September to 17.94 percent from August's 17.70 percent, fuelling fears that Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals would delay cutting interest rates or even raise them again.

- South Africa's trade performance is beginning to respond to the rand's plunge, with exports rising and imports falling in September to yield a 667 million rand surplus from 133 million rand in August.

- Claims by SAA that an employee of rival airline Comair stole vital passenger information by tapping into its computerised reservations system would have to be resolved between the two companies, Business Practices chairperson Louise Tager said on Sunday.

- International investors are expected to play a significant part in the unbundling of Malbak Ltd, which is estimated to have a value of more than 10 billion rand, with Smurfit, the Irish-based multinational paper and packaging group, tipped as a possible contender for the controlling stake in Kohler, a Malbak subsidiary.
- The 200 million rand expansion to Durban's Sapref Refinery, which is jointly owned by Shell and British Petroleum (BP), could be derailed or delayed by a backlash from the surrounding communities.

- The National Empowerment Consortium's (NEC) executive committee is set to become the driving force behind the Johnnic board, which will soon be reconstituted under the chairmanship of Cyril Ramaphosa.

- International exhibitors at the South African International Trade Exhibition (Saitex) held in Johannesburg last week expressed mixed feelings on the trade show and on doing business in South Africa.

- As Comair took to the skies in British Airways colours on Sunday, SAA announced it was temporarily reducing its domestic airfares by up to 60 percent in an attempt to gain a competitive edge in the market.

- Thousands of matriculants could be affected by the outcome of an investigation into the standards of certain papers by the South African Certification Council, the body in charge of monitoring examination standards.
- Professor Sam Nolutshungu is set to become the first black vice-chancellor of the University of the Witwatersrand.
